'''Chawne Monique Kimber''' ({{IPAc-en|ʃ|ɔː|n}} {{respell|SHAWN}};<ref name="bmck">{{Cite web |last=Allen |first=Aimee |date=17 January 2017 |title=The Beautiful Mind of Chawne Kimber |url=https://community.themodernquiltguild.com/resources/beautiful-mind-chawne-kimber |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211206053034/https://community.themodernquiltguild.com/resources/beautiful-mind-chawne-kimber |archive-date=6 December 2021 |website=Modern Quilt Guild}}</ref> born 1971)<ref name="born">{{Cite web |title=Kimber, Chawne Monique 1971- |url=https://www.worldcat.org/identities/np-kimber,%20chawne%20monique$1971/ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190923011434/https://www.worldcat.org/identities/np-kimber,%20chawne%20monique$1971/ |archive-date=23 September 2019 |access-date=22 September 2019 |website=[[WorldCat|WorldCat Identities]]}}</ref> is an [[African-American]] [[mathematician]] and [[quilter]],<ref name="mqa">{{Cite journal |last=Lamb |first=Evelyn |date=11 October 2018 |title=Math, Quilting and Activism: Mathematician Chawne Kimber shares her favorite theorems and quilts that make a statement |url=https://www.scientificamerican.com/blog/roots-of-unity/math-quilting-and-activism/ |url-status=live |journal=[[Scientific American]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240708064638/https://www.scientificamerican.com/blog/roots-of-unity/math-quilting-and-activism/ |archive-date=8 July 2024 |access-date=29 September 2024}}</ref> known for expressing her political activism in her quilts.<ref name="crq">{{Cite web |last=Hlohowskyj |first=Maria |date=2 February 2017 |title=The Colorful, Radical Quilts of Chawne Kimber |url=https://www.womenarts.org/2017/02/02/the-colorful-radical-quilts-of-chawne-kimber/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240422000722/https://www.womenarts.org/2017/02/02/the-colorful-radical-quilts-of-chawne-kimber/ |archive-date=22 April 2024 |access-date=29 September 2024 |website=Women Arts}}</ref><ref name="gelt">{{Cite news |last=Gelt |first=Jessica |date=20 February 2016 |title=These quilts with messages about gun violence and racial injustice issues aim to discomfort |url=https://www.latimes.com/entertainment/arts/la-et-cm-gun-violence-quilts-20160220-story.html |url-access=subscription |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240707220144/https://www.latimes.com/entertainment/arts/la-et-cm-gun-violence-quilts-20160220-story.html |archive-date=7 July 2024 |access-date=29 September 2024 |work=[[Los Angeles Times]]}}</ref> After working as a professor and head of mathematics at [[Lafayette College]],<ref name="profile">{{Cite web |title=Chawne Kimber |url=https://math.lafayette.edu/people/chawne-kimber/ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181012014558/https://math.lafayette.edu/people/chawne-kimber/ |archive-date=12 October 2018 |access-date=11 October 2018 |website=[[Lafayette College]]}}</ref> and as Dean of the College at [[Washington and Lee University]],<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |date=5 May 2021 |title=Chawne Kimber Named Dean of the College at Washington and Lee University |url=https://columns.wlu.edu/chawne-kimber-named-dean-of-the-college-at-washington-and-lee-university/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210506074602/https://columns.wlu.edu/chawne-kimber-named-dean-of-the-college-at-washington-and-lee-university/ |archive-date=6 May 2021 |access-date=7 June 2021 |website=The Columns |publisher=[[Washington and Lee University]] |language=en |type=Press release}}</ref> she was named as vice president for academic affairs and dean of faculty at [[Pitzer College]] in 2025.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://columns.wlu.edu/chawne-kimber-named-vice-president-for-academic-affairs-and-dean-of-faculty-at-pitzer-college/|title=Chawne Kimber Named Vice President for Academic Affairs and Dean of Faculty at Pitzer College|work=The columns|publisher=Washington and Lee University|date=March 14, 2025|access-date=2025-06-02}}</ref>

==Education and career==
Kimber, a native of [[Frankfort, Kentucky|Frankfort]], [[Kentucky]],<ref>{{Cite web |title=Artist - Chawne Kimber |url=https://americanart.si.edu/artist/chawne-kimber-32209 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240707103115/https://americanart.si.edu/artist/chawne-kimber-32209 |archive-date=7 July 2024 |access-date=29 September 2024 |website=[[Smithsonian American Art Museum]]}}</ref> comes from a family of cotton farmers and quilters in Alabama.<ref name="gelt" /><ref name="bp">{{Cite news |last=Neitz |first=Katie |date=Summer 2018 |others=Photography by Clay Wegrzynowicz |title=Beautiful and Powerful: Prof. Chawne Kimber stitches messaging about censorship, social injustice, and racism into layers of colorful cotton |url=https://magazine.lafayette.edu/summer2018/2018/07/11/beautiful-and-powerful/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240416205816/https://magazine.lafayette.edu/summer2018/2018/07/11/beautiful-and-powerful/ |archive-date=16 April 2024 |access-date=29 September 2024 |work=Lafayette Magazine |publisher=[[Lafayette College]]}}</ref> Although she writes that she "always loved math", she began her undergraduate studies at the [[University of Florida]] by studying engineering before switching to mathematics because she found it more fulfilling.<ref name="dived">{{Cite news |last=Lum |first=Lydia |date=2 May 2011 |title=Scholar Combines Math and Social Justice in the Classroom |url=https://www.diverseeducation.com/home/article/15090514/scholar-combines-math-and-social-justice-in-the-classroom |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240530183720/https://www.diverseeducation.com/home/article/15090514/scholar-combines-math-and-social-justice-in-the-classroom |archive-date=30 May 2024 |access-date=29 September 2024 |work=Diverse: Issues in Higher Education}}</ref> She earned a master's degree at the [[University of North Carolina]] in 1995, as a student of [[Idris Assani]].<ref name="bwm">{{Cite web |last=Williams |first=Scott W. |title=Chawne Kimber |url=https://www.math.buffalo.edu/mad/PEEPS/chawne_kimber.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160110201840/http://www.math.buffalo.edu/mad/PEEPS/chawne_kimber.html |archive-date=10 January 2016 |access-date=11 October 2018 |website=Black Women in Mathematics |publisher=[[University at Buffalo|State University of New York at Buffalo]]}}</ref> She returned to the University of Florida for doctoral studies, completing her Ph.D. in 1999. Her dissertation, ''Prime Ideals in Rings of Continuous Functions'', connects [[abstract algebra]] with [[functional analysis]] and was supervised by Jorge Martinez.<ref name=mgp>{{mathgenealogy|id=31099}}</ref>

After a term as Van Vleck Visiting Assistant Professor of Mathematics at Wesleyan University, she joined [[Lafayette College]] as an assistant professor. In mathematics, she is known for incorporating concepts of [[social justice]] into her classroom teaching.<ref name="dived" /><ref name="chron">{{Cite news |last=Grose |first=Ben |date=28 October 2013 |title=Adding Diversity to Curricula, Starting in the Classrooms |url=https://www.chronicle.com/article/adding-diversity-to-curricula-starting-in-the-classrooms/ |url-access=subscription |url-status=live |archive-url=https://archive.today/20231027-024041/https://www.chronicle.com/article/adding-diversity-to-curricula-starting-in-the-classrooms/ |archive-date=27 October 2023 |access-date=29 September 2024 |work=[[The Chronicle of Higher Education]]}}</ref> She was a Professor and then head of the Math Department.<ref name="profile" /> In 2008, she along with Professor Sharon Jones began the Summer Program to Advance Leadership in STEM at Lafayette.<ref name="advance">{{Cite web |date=31 October 2019 |title=Featuring the summer program to Advance Leadership in STEM @ Lafayette |url=https://citls.lafayette.edu/2019/10/31/featuring-the-summer-program-to-advance-leadership-in-stem-lafayette/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240604215041/https://citls.lafayette.edu/2019/10/31/featuring-the-summer-program-to-advance-leadership-in-stem-lafayette/ |archive-date=4 June 2024 |access-date=29 September 2024 |website=Lafayette College Center for the Integration of Teaching, Learning, and Scholarship |publisher=[[Lafayette College]]}}</ref> This six-week program where incoming students take college level writing and calculus address along with modules in STEM. Students are those who are identified as leaders from groups typically underrepresented in STEM fields.<ref name="advancing">{{Cite news |date=Winter 2010 |title=Advancing Leadership and Social Justice |url=https://www.yumpu.com/en/document/read/42191066/2010-sites-at-lafayette-lafayette-college |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240930004858/https://www.yumpu.com/en/document/read/42191066/2010-sites-at-lafayette-lafayette-college |archive-date=30 September 2024 |access-date=29 September 2024 |work=The McDonough Report |publisher=[[Lafayette College]] |pages=6–7}}</ref> In 2018, Kimber was one of six recipients of the prestigious Clare Booth Luce Scholarship to attend the HERS (Higher Education Resource Services) Institute.<ref name="hers">{{Cite web |date=5 November 2018 |title=STEM Stars |url=https://news.lafayette.edu/2018/11/05/stem-stars-2/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240709015232/https://news.lafayette.edu/2018/11/05/stem-stars-2/ |archive-date=9 July 2024 |access-date=2 June 2020 |website=[[Lafayette College]] News}}</ref> While head of the Math Department, the department "worked to promote an inclusive culture based on the understanding that math is a gateway to many other fields in the sciences, technology and engineering".<ref>{{Cite web |last=Flaherty |first=Colleen |date=19 November 2019 |title=Mathematician comes out against mandatory diversity statements, while others say they continue to be useful -- with some caveats |url=https://www.insidehighered.com/news/2019/11/19/mathematician-comes-out-against-mandatory-diversity-statements-while-others-say-they |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191119135215/http://www.insidehighered.com/news/2019/11/19/mathematician-comes-out-against-mandatory-diversity-statements-while-others-say-they |archive-date=19 November 2019 |access-date=7 June 2021 |website=[[Inside Higher Ed]] |language=en}}</ref>

In May 2021, [[Washington and Lee University]] announced that Kimber would become the school's Dean of the College effective July 1, 2021.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite web |last=Brantley |first=Max |date=4 June 2021 |title=Another win for the Lost Cause: Washington and Lee University won't change its name |url=https://arktimes.com/arkansas-blog/2021/06/04/another-win-for-the-lost-cause-washington-and-lee-university-wont-change-its-name |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231004190208/https://arktimes.com/arkansas-blog/2021/06/04/another-win-for-the-lost-cause-washington-and-lee-university-wont-change-its-name |archive-date=4 October 2023 |access-date=7 June 2021 |website=[[Arkansas Times]] |language=en-US}}</ref> She is responsible "for 21 departments and 13 interdisciplinary programs. The dean serves as chair of the Committee on Courses and Degrees and belongs to the Faculty Executive Committee. The dean reports to the provost and serves on the Provost's Academic Council as well as the President's Council".<ref name=":0" />

==Quilting==
[[File:Still not Chawne Kimber 2019.jpg|thumb|right|''still not'' (2019) at the [[Renwick Gallery]] in 2022]]
Kimber grew up with her great-grandmother's quilts<ref name="bp" /> and her father considered these "quilts his most prized possessions".<ref name=":1" /> Kimber began quilting in 2005, soon after completing her application for tenure at Lafayette, and her interest in quilting was renewed in 2007 by the death of her father.<ref name="bp" /><ref name=":1" /> Her quilts are influenced by her great-grandmother's work which "used the same patchwork style as those associated with [[Quilts of Gee's Bend|Gee's Bend]]" – Kimber views her work as a "contemporary adaptation" of that style.<ref name=":1" /> In 2008 she began creating highly politicized quilts and blogging about them,<ref name="bp" /> beginning with a series of quilts inspired by [[George Carlin]]'s [[seven dirty words]] and by racist and sexist graffiti on her college campus.<ref name="trib">{{Cite news |last=Dampier |first=Cindy |date=4 April 2017 |title=Uniting politically divided quilters, stitch by stitch |url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/2017/04/04/uniting-politically-divided-quilters-stitch-by-stitch/ |url-access=subscription |url-status=live |archive-url=https://archive.today/20240930-013104/https://www.chicagotribune.com/2017/04/04/uniting-politically-divided-quilters-stitch-by-stitch/ |archive-date=30 September 2024 |access-date=29 September 2024 |work=[[Chicago Tribune]]}}</ref><ref name="qms">{{Cite book |last=May |first=Rachel |chapter-url=https://books.google.com/books?id=TBxRAgAAQBAJ&pg=PA82 |title=Quilting with a Modern Slant: People, Patterns, and Techniques Inspiring the Modern Quilt Community |publisher=[[Workman Publishing Company|Storey Publishing]] |year=2014 |isbn=9781612120638 |location=North Adams, MA |pages=82–83 |language=en |chapter=Chawne Kimber: How Words Matter |oclc=854956985 |via=[[Google Books]]}}</ref> Her work has been associated with the "modern Quilting" movement, based on its geometric design and provocative content.<ref name="wsj">{{Cite news |last=Cox |first=Meg |date=9 May 2013 |title='Modern Quilters' Stress Simplicity, Edgy Subjects: Quilting's new-wave movement focuses on provocative material; fury at the 'F' word |url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/SB10001424127887324326504578467273484511136 |url-access=subscription |access-date=29 September 2024 |work=[[The Wall Street Journal]]}}</ref> Her work includes varied subject matter that raise social issues including the killing of African Americans and sexual assault.<ref name="trib" /> As well as quilting, Kimber has also exhibited quilting-inspired works of mathematical [[origami]].<ref name="origami">{{Cite web |date=2014 |title=Chawne Kimber and Ethan Berkove: Weaves and Whorls |url=https://gallery.bridgesmathart.org/exhibitions/2014-joint-mathematics-meetings/chawne |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231005043510/http://gallery.bridgesmathart.org/exhibitions/2014-joint-mathematics-meetings/chawne |archive-date=5 October 2023 |access-date=11 October 2018 |website=Mathematical Art Galleries: 2014 Joint Mathematics Meetings, [[The Bridges Organization]]}}</ref><ref name="cfb">{{Cite web |last1=Bruce |first1=Kathy |last2=Okaya |first2=Michiko |date=2013 |title=Crease, Fold, and Bend |url=https://galleries.lafayette.edu/wp-content/uploads/sites/99/2017/04/Crease-Fold-Bend-1.pdf |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240724094440/https://galleries.lafayette.edu/wp-content/uploads/sites/99/2017/04/Crease-Fold-Bend-1.pdf |archive-date=24 July 2024 |access-date=29 September 2024 |website=Lafayette Art Galleries |page=18}}</ref>

Kimber's quilts are frequently included at quilting shows and museum exhibits of quilting. The [[Paul Mellon Arts Center]] put up a show of her works in 2018.<ref name="bp" /><ref name="grandmother">{{Cite news |last=Bocek |first=Sasha |date=26 January 2018 |title=Not Your Grandmother's Quilt: Chawne Kimber's Radical Knits |url=https://thechoatenews.choate.edu/2018/01/26/not-grandmothers-quilt-chawne-kimbers-radical-knits/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231005043511/http://thechoatenews.choate.edu/2018/01/26/not-grandmothers-quilt-chawne-kimbers-radical-knits/ |archive-date=5 October 2023 |access-date=29 September 2024 |work=The Choate News}}</ref> One of her quilts inspired by the [[death of Eric Garner]] won first place at QuiltCon West in 2016,<ref name="gelt" /> and was included with other pieces by Kimber in a show on "Quilts and Human Rights" at the Pick Museum of Anthropology at [[Northern Illinois University]].<ref name="qhr">{{Cite web |date=25 September 2017 |title=Pick Museum unveils quilt exhibit with a visit from Reverend Jesse L. Jackson Sr. |url=https://niutoday.info/2017/09/25/pick-museum-unveils-quilt-exhibit-with-a-visit-from-reverend-jesse-l-jackson-sr/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231004190208/https://www.niutoday.info/2017/09/25/pick-museum-unveils-quilt-exhibit-with-a-visit-from-reverend-jesse-l-jackson-sr/ |archive-date=4 October 2023 |access-date=29 September 2024 |website=NIU Today, [[Northern Illinois University]]}}</ref> Her work, ''still not'', was acquired by the [[Smithsonian American Art Museum]] as part of the [[Renwick Gallery]]'s 50th Anniversary Campaign.<ref name="Savig">{{cite book |last1=Savig |first1=Mary |title=This Present Moment: Crafting a Better World |last2=Atkinson |first2=Nora |last3=Montiel |first3=Anya |publisher=[[Smithsonian American Art Museum]] |year=2022 |isbn=9781913875268 |location=Washington, DC |pages=228–238 |language=en |oclc=1291595008}}</ref><ref name="Smithsonian American Art Museum">{{cite web |title=Artworks: still not - Chawne Kimber [2019] |url=https://americanart.si.edu/artwork/still-not-118676 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240707110747/https://americanart.si.edu/artwork/still-not-118676 |archive-date=7 July 2024 |access-date=7 December 2022 |website=[[Smithsonian American Art Museum]]}}</ref> This exhibition highlighted that the piece's fabrics were "sourced from mid-century textiles".<ref name="Smithsonian American Art Museum" /> The description stated that "Kimber's choice to use vintage cloth and improvisational patterns draws on her memories and family history. Many of her enslaved ancestors in rural Alabama cultivated and ginned cotton. Her great-grandmother, Mamo, and other relatives expressed themselves through quilting. [...] Mamo's story was told through her quilts, and Kimber continues the thread".<ref name="Smithsonian American Art Museum" />

Elizabeth Landau, for ''[[The Washington Post]]'' in 2020, commented that Kimber "tries to keep her math and quilting worlds separate. Some of her quilts deliberately rebel against the patterns and orderly structures that dominate math. They are — like jazz music played with fabrics and stitches — improvisational. But the thread of challenging systemic inequalities runs through both of Kimber's endeavors. [...] Against the backdrop of persistent social injustices, Kimber's quilts are both timely and timeless".<ref name=":1">{{Cite news |last=Landau |first=Elizabeth |date=23 December 2020 |title='I can't breathe': How one Black quilter channels social justice into her work |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/lifestyle/home/social-justice-quilts-chawne-kimber/2020/12/22/0f517ab8-205f-11eb-b532-05c751cd5dc2_story.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://archive.today/20201223-194923/https://www.washingtonpost.com/lifestyle/home/social-justice-quilts-chawne-kimber/2020/12/22/0f517ab8-205f-11eb-b532-05c751cd5dc2_story.html |archive-date=23 December 2020 |access-date=30 March 2023 |newspaper=[[The Washington Post]] |language=en-US |issn=0190-8286}}</ref>
